WoW: Forever

Hunter

Misdirection does not exist, pets now inherit your stats, and Survival became a genuine melee spec. Hunter has 110 changes in the client diff — more than any other class.

  1. Home
  2. WoW: Forever
  3. Hunter

Start with a correction

Several guides report that Auto Shot is no longer clipped by abilities. That is a bug Blizzard is reverting. From the community manager on 23 September: "the 0.5-second cast time that precedes a Hunter's auto-shot or the use of a wand is not functioning properly... this is something that we will fix in an upcoming Beta build." The 0.5-second cast is intended, and as of 30 September the fix had not shipped. It is tempting to read the revert as a win for player feedback — the thread "Hunter is ruined" was edited to "WE ARE SAVED" when it was announced. That was its author alone. Blizzard's own announcement thread drew 136 replies overwhelmingly asking Blizzard not to fix it: "Hunters currently feel so incredibly smooth to the point that the class should be balanced around this bug rather than reverting back to its clunky Classic version."

Misdirection: confirmed absent

Zero occurrences in the client-read spellbook diff — not among new, changed or unchanged spells. It is a Burning Crusade ability with no vanilla ancestor to diff against. One guide names it once in an introduction and never again in 800 lines; that is boilerplate, not evidence. Hunters have no threat-transfer tool in Forever, and neither does anyone else.

Pets inherit your stats

The single most consequential change for level 60. The system is confirmed; the coefficients are player-derived, because the client does not expose them.

Your statWhat the pet gets
Stamina2 pet health per point
Armor30% of yours
Attack Power10% of your highest source
Critical Strike100% of yours

That crit line roughly doubles the value of crit for Beast Mastery. Other pet changes. A new Fox family with Trickster's Dance. Owl renamed Bird of Prey. Eight families got new abilities — Bear Swipe hits three targets and is the AoE-threat pick. Focus regeneration roughly doubled to about 10 per second, continuous. Furious Howl was rebuilt into a one-minute party buff, then nerfed 40%. Loyalty still exists, still gates training, and rises very slowly — but once you learn an ability you can teach it to any future pet. Two things to watch. All pets swing at a base 2.0 seconds with a passive restoring the classic speed, and damage is not normalized to speed, so a fast pet is simply better and nobody knows if that is intended. And unlearning pet training points also unlearns the attack-speed passive, permanently changing your pet's swing. Do not trust the common claim that happiness decays much more slowly — part of what testers measured was a bug where happiness stopped decreasing at max loyalty, fixed on 24 September.

Talents

Beast MasteryBestial SwiftnessSummon HawkIntimidationBestial Wrath
MarksmanshipLone WolfTrueshot AuraScatter ShotSniper Shot
SurvivalDeterrenceCounterattackStrider KickLacerating Strikes

Marksmanship got the most interesting new talent in the class. Lone Wolf, at 11 points: "You deal 20% increased damage with all attacks while you do not have an active pet." That makes petless Marksmanship a real build for the first time in vanilla's lineage. Careful Aim gives +20% of your Intellect as generic attack power. Aimed Shot is no longer a talent — it is trained. Survival is the real rework. Improved Tracking gives +1% damage per rank against whatever creature type you are tracking. Entrapment was rewritten from a 5% chance of a 5-second root into "when your traps are triggered, all affected targets are Entrapped" — a guaranteed root that is on-demand with no diminishing returns. Survival Tactics makes trap resistance a hit problem, which is the mechanical hook for Blizzard's stated trap-reliability rationale. And Expose Prey gives attacks against a marked target a chance to activate Mongoose Bite, finally unchaining it from being dodge-only. Removed: Wyvern Sting, Improved Feign Death, Humanoid Slaying, Killer Instinct.

Abilities

Traps are usable in combat. The out-of-combat clause is deleted from all four tooltips, cooldowns went 15 to 30 seconds, and exclusivity is now per school — one Fire and one Frost trap should coexist, though a bug currently prevents it. Aimed Shot and Multi-Shot now share a 6-second cooldown, which collapses the Marksmanship rotation into a single node. Aimed Shot's cast dropped to 2 seconds and its flat bonus damage was slashed hard — rank 6 from 600 to 166. Multi-Shot lost ranks 2 through 5 entirely. Serpent Sting now scales with ranged attack power, can crit, and is dynamic rather than snapshotted. Scorpid Sting was rewritten to reduce the target's hit chance by 2%. Volley lost its one-minute cooldown. Aspect of the Beast is now a damage aspect, and Aspect of the Monkey gained a 100-yard range so the pet benefits from it. Disengage is still the vanilla melee-range threat dump, not the retail leap. The dead zone is still in the game — 0 to 8 yards — and Blizzard has made no statement about it despite four heavy threads.

Rotation

At 20 all three specs are identical, because nothing has diverged: Hunter's Mark, let the pet attack first, Serpent Sting, Aimed Shot on cooldown, Auto Shot filler, Disengage if you steal aggro, Arcane Shot only when mana-capped, Multi-Shot against several targets. At 60, derived from tooltips and never played: Beast Mastery revolves around keeping two hawks up, so Arcane Shot becomes the filler you use when a hawk would be wasted. Marksmanship is the shared 6-second node plus maintained Serpent Sting — Sniper Shot is situational, not rotational, and one guide judges its cast time may make it a damage loss in PvE. Survival is genuinely melee: react to Mongoose Bite windows, Strider Kick on cooldown, traps woven with Resourcefulness paying the mana. Dual wield is not mandatory — Strider Kick scales with weapon damage, which testers say makes two-handers viable rather than stat sticks. A Survival landmine: beta players report melee attacks currently reset the ranged swing timer, badly affecting weaving, and it is unclear whether that is intended. Traps also do not scale with attack power, which caps the trap-centric build.

Stats

At 20: weapon damage far above everything, then Agility. Prefer slower, higher-damage weapons because Aimed Shot derives from weapon damage. At 60: weapon damage, Agility, then Hit — which is worth more to a Forever Hunter than a Classic one, because one stat now buys melee hit, ranged hit, trap reliability and Feign Death reliability. Then crit, which transfers 100% to your pet. Separate ranged weapon skills survive. Bows, Crossbows and Guns are still distinct, and at 300 skill the effective hit cap against bosses is 9%, with 5 weapon skill worth roughly 3% hit. The stat on items was gutted while the skill stayed intact, so the practical route to the cap is now hit itself.

Race

The weapon-specialization crit racials do not work for ranged attacks, and this is the most important race fact in the class. In-game stat-window screenshots settled what the guides disagreed about: Human Sword, Orc Axe and Dwarf Mace Specialization feed your pet, your melee, Arcane Shot and Serpent Sting — but not Aimed Shot, Multi-Shot or Auto Shot. The decisive comparison is that Elune's Light carries the same "all spells and attacks" wording and does apply to ranged. A player put this to Blizzard directly and got no reply, so whether it is a bug or the design is unknown. As it stands, the newly-added Human Hunter gets nothing from its own racial. Tauren is called the single strongest choice across both factions — Endurance now grants +5% health and +1% hit, and Plainsrunning lets you stutter-step-kite from level 1 while keeping Aspect of the Hawk up. Night Elf is the Alliance pick, on Elune's Light and Shadowmeld now working in combat. Dwarf Hunter is a real grievance across three threads — Gun Specialization is gone, replaced by a crit racial on a weapon class Hunters cannot use.

Sentiment

Mostly aimed at preserved vanilla friction rather than the new design. Lone Wolf, melee Survival, hawks, in-combat traps and pet scaling are broadly welcomed. The anger is at the dead zone, stable slots ("basically a deal breaker for me personally"), quivers and ammo pouches, Dwarf racials, and the fact that the tame-to-learn-pet-skills system is never explained in-game. One balance pass touched Hunter, on 24 September: Furious Howl −40%, a Tame Beast anti-exploit, two bug fixes, and a Strider Kick buff. That is all of it.

Still unknown

Whether weapon-spec racial crit is meant to exclude ranged. Exact pet inheritance coefficients. Whether pet damage normalization to speed is intended. Whether the Auto Shot revert has shipped. And Black Arrow, which the client diff lists as an unchanged Hunter spell despite no vanilla equivalent existing — most likely a data artefact.
